assumptions.statement: V_l is finite with no uniform upper bound, and X_l is the finite product of standard-Borel coordinate spaces.
rho_l is a probability law, m_l=exp(-H_l)rho_l has finite strictly positive mass, and pi_l is its normalization.
K_l is normalized, positive, measurable, and parameter independent; rho_l K_l and m_l K_l define the next measure pair.
A fixed jointly measurable reverse-kernel version Pi_l(dx|z) disintegrates pi_l(dx)K_l(x,dz).
The nonlinear action chart is an open L-infinity ball; every required exponential and derivative is uniformly bounded there.
The interaction tier has finite product structure, a covariant product probability nu_l equivalent to pi_l, and all nonempty subset interactions in hierarchical zero-mean gauge.
Each retained interaction space is closed and has a declared bounded idempotent projection with a declared operator norm and quotient residual norm.
One principal G-bundle induces belief and model statistical bundles; actions, references, kernels, sections, connections, and scale morphisms carry the stated equivariance data.
Statistical paths are differentiable in quadratic mean with centered finite-L2 scores, and parameter-independent pushforwards stay in the selected coarse family.
For the explicit spectral realization, X_i are iid N(0,1), b>=2, Z=b^(-1/2)sum_i X_i, and Hermites use the normalized probabilists' convention.
Ordinary spectra, fixed points, and beta differences use declared bounded scale isomorphisms J_l to one normed reference object.
Generalized mode sections have fixed norm, sign or phase, and per-volume normalization; only tempered scale-gauge changes are admitted as equivalences.
Q_l is a smooth regular configuration manifold with declared Fisher metric and a locally existing unique VFE vector field; the coarse configuration map is separately smooth.
The admitted probability family has a fixed sigma-finite dominating measure, jointly measurable density representatives, common support controls, and justified integral or derivative exchanges.
The extended ELBO uses fixed evidence, declared Radon-Nikodym representatives, extended-real conventions, and the exact H4 boundary for the integrated identity.
Every external theorem or attribution uses a checked primary source or authoritative monograph with an exact statement and hypothesis mapping.
Numerical stability claims use deterministic controls through condition number 10^14, high-precision comparisons, scale-aware error bounds, and machine-readable JUnit output.
Verification binds the complete declared input policy, separates update from nonmutating verify mode, and records source revision, UTC timestamp, and semantic payload digest.
Scale depth l, inference-orbit coordinate r, Fisher duration, and physical time are distinct; a shared fine/coarse history requires a positive oriented semiconjugacy factor.

claims.statement: For every finite standard-Borel agent network of arbitrary finite cardinality, every finite interaction hypergraph on it, and every normalized parameter-independent blocking channel satisfying the declared domination, product-factor, gauge-equivariance, smoothness, and integrability hypotheses, construct a typed scale-indexed measure-pair, action, full-interaction, score-tangent, bundle, configuration, and history theory whose exact coarse maps, derivatives, contractions, defects, generalized modes, cocycles, beta data, fixed objects, pullback compatibilities, extended ELBO identities, and exact-versus-projected boundaries satisfy the obligations atomized in the bound claim ledger.
claims.quantifiers: For every finite vertex set V_l with no upper bound on |V_l|; every finite standard-Borel product space X_l=product_{i in V_l} X_{l,i}; every finite interaction hypergraph; every probability reference rho_l; every finite positive likelihood measure m_l=exp(-H_l)rho_l; every normalized parameter-independent Markov kernel K_l:X_l rightsquigarrow X_{l+1} admitted by the stated hypotheses; every declared principal G-bundle, pair of associated statistical bundles, compatible scale morphism, DQM score path, full Hoeffding interaction, retained projection, regular configuration manifold, and selected fine history meeting its local assumptions; and every finite composable sequence of such scales.
claims.falsifier: An admitted finite typed instance that violates any universal conjunct, or any unresolved load-bearing ancestor, blocks affirmative closure.

claims.statement: The normalized kernel defines rho_{l+1}=rho_l K_l, m_{l+1}=m_l K_l, and R_l^H=-log(d m_{l+1}/d rho_{l+1}) as an extended measure-level action wherever the derivative exists.
claims.quantifiers: Every scale l and every pair and kernel satisfying H-MEASURE and H-MARKOV.
claims.falsifier: A normalized admitted kernel for which domination or the Radon-Nikodym action fails under the recorded hypotheses.

claims.statement: Q_l(phi)=R_l^H[H_l+phi]-R_l^H[H_l] is locally real analytic from an open L-infinity ball to L-infinity(pi_{l+1}).
claims.quantifiers: Every l and every phi in the declared open ball under H-REVERSE and H-CHART.
claims.falsifier: An admitted bounded increment for which the conditional log-Laplace map leaves L-infinity or lacks a convergent local derivative expansion.

claims.statement: D R_l^H(H_l)[phi]=E[phi|Z] and D^2 R_l^H(H_l)[phi,psi]=-Cov(phi,psi|Z) as bounded typed maps between the declared action spaces.
claims.quantifiers: Every l and bounded phi,psi under H-REVERSE and H-CHART.
claims.falsifier: A valid finite kernel whose difference quotient disagrees with the conditional mean or whose second derivative disagrees with minus conditional covariance.

claims.statement: U_l extends uniquely to a contraction Lp(pi_l) to Lp(pi_{l+1}) for every 1<=p<=infinity and preserves means for finite p.
claims.quantifiers: Every l, every 1<=p<=infinity, and every phi in Lp(pi_l).
claims.falsifier: A normalized parameter-independent admitted kernel with ||E[phi|Z]||_p>||phi||_p.

claims.statement: ||phi||_2^2-||U_l phi||_2^2=E Var(phi|Z)>=0, with the loss equal to the conditional score variance.
claims.quantifiers: Every l and phi in L2(pi_l).
claims.falsifier: A square-integrable admitted tangent for which total conditional variance fails.

claims.statement: Because U_l 1=1 and the nonlinear map is additively homogeneous, both descend to action quotients by constants while evidence mass remains a separately tracked scalar.
claims.quantifiers: Every l under H-MARKOV and the explicitly projective tier.
claims.falsifier: Two representatives differing by a constant whose coarse actions fail to differ by the same constant.

claims.statement: On L-infinity/R1 with oscillation norm, ||overline(U_l)||<=delta_l; strict nonautonomous irrelevance follows only from negative accumulated log-delta growth relative to accumulated block scale.
claims.quantifiers: Every l with the fixed reverse-kernel version and every finite cocycle segment; asymptotic conclusion only when B_{n<-l} tends to infinity and the displayed limsup is negative.
claims.falsifier: A bounded quotient function exceeding the Dobrushin oscillation bound, or a one-step delta<1 example with nonnegative long-run normalized cocycle growth.

claims.statement: For a bounded positive unital operator on the declared complex Banach lattice with quasi-interior unit and the recorded pole/eigenfunctional hypothesis, r(U)>1 implies r(U)=r_ess(U).
claims.quantifiers: Every operator satisfying the full Banach-lattice and pole hypotheses.
claims.falsifier: An operator meeting every hypothesis with r(U)>1 but r(U)>r_ess(U), or a missing strict-positivity step for the dual eigenfunctional.

claims.statement: For Uf=f composed with circle doubling, r(U)=1 on L-infinity and r(U)=2^alpha on periodic C^alpha with the sup-plus-Holder norm for 0<alpha<=1.
claims.quantifiers: Every 0<alpha<=1 for the specified Haar circle kernel.
claims.falsifier: Failure of the 2^(alpha n) upper bound or of the matching Fourier-mode lower bound.

claims.statement: Hierarchical zero-mean extraction P_l and assembly E_l are bounded inverse maps between the full nonempty Hoeffding interaction space and the bounded action quotient.
claims.quantifiers: Every arbitrary finite V_l under H-INTERACTION.
claims.falsifier: A bounded action class whose power-set extraction fails to reconstruct it modulo constants or a normalized interaction not recovered by extraction.

claims.statement: The product reference nu_l is gauge covariant and equivalent to pi_l at every admitted scale, preserving null sets and the hierarchical normalization used by extraction.
claims.quantifiers: Every l and every admitted gauge change and scale arrow.
claims.falsifier: A gauge or scale arrow that changes null sets, destroys product covariance, or violates zero-mean normalization.

claims.statement: R_l^G=P_{l+1} overline(R_l^H) E_l is the exact full-interaction coarse map and M_l=P_{l+1} overline(U_l) E_l is its typed derivative along the exact orbit.
claims.quantifiers: Every l and g_l in the full finite interaction space under H-INTERACTION.
claims.falsifier: An induced higher-order term missing from the claimed exact output or a derivative whose domain and codomain do not match adjacent tangent spaces.

claims.statement: R_{l,Q}^G=Q_{l+1}P_{l+1}overline(R_l^H)E_l is projected, and the omitted quotient residual is exactly (I-E_{l+1}Q_{l+1}P_{l+1})overline(R_l^H)(E_l g_l); it vanishes for all retained inputs exactly when the retained space is invariant.
claims.quantifiers: Every declared retained subspace and input under H-PROJECTION.
claims.falsifier: A nonzero omitted residual labeled exact, or a claimed invariant retained space with a nonzero residual.

claims.statement: The iid product DQM score is E_b h=sum_i h(X_i), the coarse pushed score is L_b h=E[E_b h|Z], and every centered L2 h is realized by the stated squared linear density path.
claims.quantifiers: Every centered h in L2(mu_*) and integer b>=2.
claims.falsifier: A centered L2 h for which the path is not normalized or lacks DQM score h, or whose product/pushforward score differs from the formulas.

claims.statement: At the Gaussian fixed law, L_b e_k=b^(1-k/2)e_k and the centered L2 spectrum is {b^(1-k/2):k>=1} union {0}; k=1 is relevant, k=2 marginal, and k>=3 irrelevant under the fixed norm and block convention.
claims.quantifiers: Every integer b>=2 and normalized probabilists' Hermite index k>=1.
claims.falsifier: A Hermite mode violating the Mehler conditional-expectation identity or incompleteness of the claimed spectral closure.

claims.statement: Cross-scale mode equations are typed as M_l v_{l,a}=lambda_{l,a}v_{l+1,a}, or transported to a reference endomorphism; exponent invariance requires both tempered scalar mode normalization and tempered distortion of the complete comparison trivialization and its inverse.
claims.quantifiers: Every exact interaction orbit, comparison trivialization, and mode section satisfying H-MODE and H-REFERENCE; exponent conclusions only when the limit or stated limsup exists.
claims.falsifier: An ordinary eigen-equation across unequal spaces, or the identity cocycle equipped with superexponentially distorted scale norms that changes the apparent exponent.

claims.statement: Composed exact derivatives and normalized generalized eigenvalues satisfy the ordered cross-scale cocycle law lambda_{n<-l,a}=product_{k=l}^{n-1}lambda_{k,a}; an autonomous semigroup is asserted only after compatible stationary identifications.
claims.quantifiers: Every finite composable scale segment and normalized invariant line.
claims.falsifier: A composable segment for which ordered derivative composition or scalar multiplication fails, or semigroup language without stationary identification.

claims.statement: Nonautonomous scale diagrams use invariant sections in each typed tier; an ordinary fixed point is formed only after the scale maps become endomorphisms of one declared reference object.
claims.quantifiers: Every admitted nonautonomous diagram and every tier named in the statement.
claims.falsifier: A fixed-point subtraction or equality whose operands inhabit distinct spaces without a declared identification.

claims.statement: The discrete interaction beta is [J_{l+1}^{-1}R_l^GJ_l(g)-g]/log b_l; any continuous covariant scale derivative requires a separate smooth scale manifold, Banach bundle, interpolation, and scale connection unrelated to the contextual gauge connection.
claims.quantifiers: Every l with b_l>1 and declared reference isomorphisms; continuous claim only under the stated extension.
claims.falsifier: A beta subtraction between unequal spaces or a continuous derivative without the required smooth bundle data.

claims.statement: The score is S_{l,H}[phi]=-(phi-E_pi phi), an isometric isomorphism from L2/R1 with Fisher norm to L2_0, and S_{l+1,R_lH}[U_l phi]=E[S_{l,H}[phi]|Z].
claims.quantifiers: Every l and phi in L2(pi_l).
claims.falsifier: A representative dependence after quotienting or a failure of the centered conditional-expectation square.

claims.statement: For a smooth parameter-independent normalized Markov fiber morphism Psi_l, Delta_F=g_l^F-(T^V Psi_l)^*g_{l+1}^F is positive semidefinite and equals conditional score covariance.
claims.quantifiers: Every selected DQM fine/coarse family and vertical tangent under H-GAUGE and H-DQM.
claims.falsifier: An admitted parameter-independent fiber map that increases Fisher norm or lacks the stated vertical tangent type.

claims.statement: A cross-scale associated-bundle morphism is globally defined only after the principal map is G-equivariant and the smooth statistical-law fiber map intertwines the represented G-actions; the sample-space kernel and induced law-manifold map remain distinct typed objects.
claims.quantifiers: Every adjacent scale arrow and both belief and model channels.
claims.falsifier: Two representatives of one associated-bundle point that map to different target classes because the fiber intertwining equation fails.

claims.statement: Composable base maps, principal maps, law-fiber maps, and associated-bundle morphisms satisfy their ordered identity and composition laws before the scale family is called a functor or cocycle.
claims.quantifiers: Every finite composable sequence of scale arrows and both associated channels.
claims.falsifier: A pair of admitted adjacent arrows whose composed bundle morphism differs from the declared direct arrow.

claims.statement: The covariant first-jet chain rule retains the vertical horizontal-defect term, its exact composition law, and every signed cross term in the base Fisher comparison; positivity follows only when that defect vanishes.
claims.quantifiers: Every related fine/coarse section and tangent under H-GAUGE.
claims.falsifier: The trivial line-bundle identity map with source horizontal field d/dx and target horizontal field d/dx+a d/dy, for which the uncorrected fine-minus-coarse base tensor is negative.

claims.statement: Related sections and horizontal-lift-compatible bundle morphisms pull the vertical Fisher defect to h_l^omega-f_l^*h_{l+1}^{omega'}>=0; without the commutative first-jet square, the vertical mismatch term is retained.
claims.quantifiers: Every l, base tangent, and related section satisfying H-GAUGE and the compatibility square.
claims.falsifier: A claimed defect pullback when sections are unrelated, horizontal lifts fail to commute, or the omitted mismatch is nonzero.

claims.statement: Each configuration manifold is an explicitly selected finite-dimensional or Banach/Hilbert section manifold, and its strong Fisher metric is either the pullback of a declared joint-law Fisher metric or a labeled weighted product metric with base measure, channel weights, gauge quotient, finiteness, and nondegeneracy data.
claims.quantifiers: Every scale at which a natural-gradient vector field or Fisher duration is asserted.
claims.falsifier: An all-smooth-sections space with no manifold topology, a weak metric with no gradient, or a weighted marginal metric labeled the exact joint Fisher metric without block orthogonality.

claims.statement: The configuration coarse map from Q_l to Q_{l+1} is separately typed, symbolically disambiguated, and smooth; it is not identified with the law, action, interaction, reference-space, or bundle coarse map.
claims.quantifiers: Every l for which a configuration-level history comparison is made.
claims.falsifier: A history theorem using an abstract kernel with no smooth tangent map, or a configuration symbol already assigned to a reference-space endomorphism.

claims.statement: A pointwise bundle morphism induces a configuration coarse map only after the transformed fine section is constant on fibers of the base coarse map and smooth descent is proved, or after a separate smooth gauge-equivariant averaging or variational construction is supplied.
claims.quantifiers: Every admitted fine section when a pointwise-induced configuration map is asserted.
claims.falsifier: The base collapse S1 to a point with identity fiber map and fine section Q(x)=sin x, which cannot descend to a section over the point.

claims.statement: Independently recomputed fine and coarse VFE vector fields share an oriented orbit only if T Rhat_l X_l=a_l(X_{l+1} composed with Rhat_l) with a_l>0; otherwise only a fine path and its pushforward are compared.
claims.quantifiers: Every l and every configuration in the domain under H-CONFIG and H-HISTORY.
claims.falsifier: A shared-history claim with a nonpositive factor, a failed tangent equality, or an independently optimized coarse orbit not related by semiconjugacy.

claims.statement: A nonconstant shared oriented history additionally requires a nonzero pushed vector field on every regular subarc and appropriate maximal-interval conditions; semiconjugacy alone may collapse every fine orbit to a point.
claims.quantifiers: Every fine orbit for which nonconstant or global shared-history language is used.
claims.falsifier: A constant configuration coarse map with a zero coarse vector field, which satisfies the semiconjugacy equation but collapses nonconstant fine orbits.

claims.statement: Under semiconjugacy the exact fine and coarse Fisher speeds are recorded separately; duration equality requires configuration-metric compatibility along the orbit and does not follow from fiberwise Fisher contraction.
claims.quantifiers: Every regular semiconjugate orbit segment with finite configuration Fisher speeds.
claims.falsifier: The identity map and identical vector fields on R with metrics dx^2 and 4 dx^2, for which semiconjugacy holds while coarse duration is twice fine duration.

claims.statement: The canonical relative-log extended ELBO is defined on the declared measure-level domain and yields fixed-evidence monotonicity with an explicit distinction between the unconditional extended statement and the H4-dependent integrated ELBO.
claims.quantifiers: Every admitted law under H-PROBABILITY and H-ELBO, including extended-real cases named by the definition.
claims.falsifier: An admitted fixed-evidence case in which the definition is undefined, changes with density version, or the monotonicity proof uses H4 without stating it.

claims.statement: All parameter and configuration laws use one fixed family-level sigma-finite dominating reference; mixed coordinates use a fixed countable atomic support covering the admitted family.
claims.quantifiers: Every admitted parameter and configuration in the probability family.
claims.falsifier: The moving-atom family mu_theta=0.5 delta_theta+0.5 N(0,1), or another admitted family with no common sigma-finite dominator.

claims.statement: Probability-kernel integration is separated from integration against a fixed sigma-finite measure, and every likelihood density used jointly in parameters and observations is a declared jointly measurable version.
claims.quantifiers: Every kernel, density, and integral used by the probability and ELBO chapters.
claims.falsifier: A pointwise density version valid for each parameter but not jointly measurable, or use of a probability-kernel lemma for an infinite sigma-finite integration measure.

claims.statement: R_i^x is defined at first use with its source, target, and passive frame-change direction, and every later gauge formula uses the same convention.
claims.quantifiers: Every channel x, agent i, overlap, and gauge change in the revised source.
claims.falsifier: A three-frame composition or transformed density using the reciprocal convention without an explicit change of variables.

claims.statement: The measure-level pushforward law is general; the determinant density formula is asserted only for the Lebesgue or declared relatively invariant reference tier.
claims.quantifiers: Every represented gauge action and reference measure.
claims.falsifier: A mixed continuous-atomic reference for which the determinant law is claimed despite failed relative invariance.

claims.statement: The design-dependent shared-link admissible rechoices are called a constraint-preserving family unless closure is proved; the actual context-independent subgroup remains separately identified.
claims.quantifiers: Every finite design and shared-link constraint.
claims.falsifier: The recorded GL(2,R) pair whose product leaves the claimed stabilizer, or any admitted nonclosure witness.

claims.statement: The Gaussian interaction energy kernel is positive semidefinite with its exact null-space criterion, while the constructive nonempty normalized-density witness requires every self precision A_i to be positive definite.
claims.quantifiers: Every finite interaction graph with positive-semidefinite edge weights and the stated self-term hypotheses.
claims.falsifier: The zero-self consensus-nullspace witness, or a claimed normalized Gaussian with singular precision.

claims.statement: The nonnormalized information-metric attribution records Campbell's mass-dependent two-function family rather than uniqueness up to one constant scale.
claims.quantifiers: The exact nonnormalized-measure theorem and the manuscript sentence that cites it.
claims.falsifier: A checked primary-source statement proving uniqueness up to a single scale under the manuscript's exact hypotheses.

claims.statement: The cited Jona-Lasinio source is mapped hypothesis by hypothesis for conditional expectation as RG linearization, generalized tangent-space eigenvalues, and their cocycle law.
claims.quantifiers: Each imported equation and every manuscript application.
claims.falsifier: A source/applicability mismatch in state space, normalization, fixed law, tangent type, or scale composition.

claims.statement: PB-1 through PB-4 are rerun against the repaired source and a current closure ledger cites only paths existing at its bound revision; the stale historical record is not relabeled.
claims.quantifiers: Each PB claim and every cited source location in the new ledger.
claims.falsifier: A cited path absent from git ls-tree at the bound revision or any retained stale artifact revision.

claims.statement: The Gaussian determinant gap is evaluated through Schur canonical correlations using triangular solves and log1p, telescopes along a declared refinement tree, and passes the recorded high-condition controls without unconditional clipping.
claims.quantifiers: All declared dimensions, blockings, and condition-number controls under H-NUMERICAL.
claims.falsifier: A stable high-precision control outside the derived error bound, a negative gap beyond rounding allowance, or JUnit failure/error.

claims.statement: Verify mode compares rather than rewrites the bound result, records UTC time, source revision and semantic digest, covers every declared input class, and fails on missing, malformed, unexpected, mutated, or revision-mismatched inputs.
claims.quantifiers: Every bound input class and every mutation control in H-MANIFEST.
claims.falsifier: Any mutation that verifies successfully or any verify invocation that changes the verified result bytes.

claims.statement: Chapter 12 no longer credits Chapter 2 with a deleted averaged-connection proof; the operational-trace statement is separately conjectural and the orphan label is removed.
claims.quantifiers: Every affected sentence, label, and status tag.
claims.falsifier: A source scan finding the stale attribution, orphan label, or missing conjectural status.

claims.statement: The relative principal-frame field h_i and graph gauge changes h_i^x are reconciled without type collision, and the two inverse transformation laws use one declared orientation.
claims.quantifiers: Every occurrence in source and notation appendix.
claims.falsifier: A static/type scan finding an unreconciled h use or reciprocal law.

claims.statement: Chapter 9 defines B, B_perp, G, Q, and pdet before use, and Q is disambiguated from recognition-law notation.
claims.quantifiers: Every affected Chapter 9 occurrence and notation entry.
claims.falsifier: A definition-before-use or collision scan that finds an unresolved symbol.

claims.statement: The evidence-preserving channel theorem states K(x,Y)=1 as the hypothesis used by its display, rather than the weaker statement that the kernel does not read Q_o.
claims.quantifiers: Every kernel admitted by that theorem.
claims.falsifier: A sub-Markov counterexample admitted by the revised hypotheses or a missing normalization clause.

claims.statement: The compact holonomy statement uses the closure of represented holonomy wherever the finitely generated image need not be closed.
claims.quantifiers: Every finite graph represented holonomy family in the affected result.
claims.falsifier: A nonclosed finitely generated represented holonomy for which the unrepaired compactness argument fails.

claims.statement: The notation appendix includes the complete typed RG operator tier and distinguishes its symbols from unrelated R and c uses.
claims.quantifiers: Every RG symbol used by the repaired chapters.
claims.falsifier: A symbol inventory finding an RG operator absent or multiply typed without a disambiguation clause.

claims.statement: Measure-pair composition requires composable normalized kernels and not a spurious nested-forest condition.
claims.quantifiers: Every finite composable sequence of admitted kernels.
claims.falsifier: Two composable normalized kernels whose measure pushforwards fail associativity.

claims.statement: The two additive constants formerly named c_b are given distinct symbols and types: evidence-mass normalization versus fixed-ray or scale normalization.
claims.quantifiers: Every affected equation and notation entry.
claims.falsifier: A remaining occurrence where one glyph is used for both types without explicit scope.

claims.statement: The lumpability biconditional and the memory-operator identity cite checked Kemeny-Snell and Nakajima-Zwanzig primary or authoritative sources with mapped hypotheses.
claims.quantifiers: Each cited theorem and manuscript use.
claims.falsifier: A source mismatch or an exact biconditional asserted under weaker conditions than the cited theorem.

claims.statement: The result presently mislabeled Tauberian is named Abelian unless a genuine converse with its added hypotheses is proved.
claims.quantifiers: The affected theorem and every cross-reference.
claims.falsifier: A source/status scan retaining the Tauberian name without a proved converse.

claims.statement: Chapter 11 points the cut-closure condition to its actual labeled equation in Chapter 9.
claims.quantifiers: Every affected cross-reference.
claims.falsifier: A resolved-reference audit showing the pointer still lands on the wrong result.

claims.statement: The Esfeld citation is narrowed to the thesis the checked source supports and no longer attributes the stronger radical structural-realist position that it rejects.
claims.quantifiers: Every Esfeld-dependent sentence.
claims.falsifier: A primary-source passage contradicting the revised attribution or surviving stronger claim.

claims.statement: The van Fraassen citation is narrowed so constructive empiricism is not presented as an eliminative idle-wheel parsimony rule it does not state.
claims.quantifiers: Every van-Fraassen-dependent sentence.
claims.falsifier: A primary-source audit showing the revised prose still exceeds the source.

claims.statement: The PDF keyword metadata removes or explicitly reconciles emergent time with the manuscript's refusal to identify information duration or RG depth with physical time.
claims.quantifiers: The released metadata and every scope disclaimer.
claims.falsifier: A metadata/source scan finding the unreconciled keyword.

claims.statement: Each multi-claim paragraph has one visibly scoped status per governed claim; the RG relevance trichotomy is DEFINITION, and the operational-trace statement is CONJECTURE.
claims.quantifiers: Every affected paragraph and status entry.
claims.falsifier: A status scan finding stacked tags with ambiguous scope or an ESTABLISHED tag on the trichotomy definition.

claims.statement: Status tags render as unbreakable units and no released page hyphenates a status token across lines.
claims.quantifiers: Every rendered status tag in the released PDF.
claims.falsifier: A visual or text-extraction audit finding a broken status token.

claims.statement: Generated auxiliary files are ignored or freshly produced in the release build and no stale tracked auxiliary is treated as current evidence.
claims.quantifiers: Every generated TeX auxiliary and release build.
claims.falsifier: A stale tracked auxiliary influencing or misdescribing the released build.
